INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.

Project Background

GGGI works in partnership with countries around the world to strengthen their capacity and advance green growth policies and investments that can positively impact the lives of millions of people. The organization collaborates with national governments, multilateral institutions, public agencies, and the private sector to support the development of economies that are robust, resource-efficient, low-carbon, and resilient to climate change.

GGGI implements a diverse portfolio of programs across developing countries. Through these in-country initiatives, complemented by global products and services, the organization delivers results through an integrated approach that combines evidence-based policy planning, technical assistance, and investment facilitation, aligned with national development priorities. GGGI also promotes knowledge generation and management activities that strengthen the theoretical and empirical foundations of green growth, provide practical guidance for policymakers, and help create enabling conditions for both public and private green investments.

In Colombia, GGGI has been working closely with the national government since 2014 to advance green growth policies and investments. The organization has established strategic partnerships with institutions such as the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, and the National Planning Department (DNP), among others.

Within the framework of the UK PACT (Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions) Bio Rural Project (2024–2027), the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), the Government of Antioquia, and the Caja de Compensación Familiar de Antioquia – COMFAMA signed a Special Cooperation Agreement to implement the initiative "Antioquia BioCompetitiva." The project seeks to accelerate the scaling of innovative bioeconomy solutions in the Department of Antioquia through two strategic components: (I) promoting knowledge transfer and capacity-building processes, with a focus on circular bioeconomy and the internationalization of bioproducts; and (II) strengthening productive, technological, and commercial capacities within the department through an integrated value-chain development approach.

Under the second component, three calls for proposals will be implemented to accelerate the development of the bioeconomy ecosystem while strengthening strategic value chains in the department. These calls include:
Bioeconomy acceleration support for microenterprises affiliated with COMFAMA.
Investment scaling support for four companies linked to bioeconomy value chains.

Agrovizcaya Finca Viva seeks to strengthen its biofactory through the support of the design and implementation of an integrated management system that standardizes production processes, ensures product quality, upgrades infrastructure, establishes a traceability system, and prepares the organization to meet the regulatory requirements of the Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) for the production and commercialization of organic fertilizers, soil conditioners, and agricultural bioinputs.
OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The objective of this consultancy is to provide specialized technical support the articulation, documentation alignment and monitoring of the Integrated Management System (IMS) documentation of Agrovizcaya Finca Viva's biofactory, and monitoring the phased implementation under the Antioquia BioCompetitiva Project, providing technical guidance and recommendations to support the company's readiness for its registration processes before the Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) for the production and commercialization of organic fertilizers, soil conditioners, and agricultural bioinputs.
DELIVERABLES AND PAYMENT SCHEDULE

Under the overall supervision of the GGGI Colombia team, and in direct coordination with the beneficiary company, Agrovizcaya Finca Viva, the Consultant will coordinate and provide specialized technical support for the alignment of the biofactory's Integrated Management System, consolidated for monitoring and payment purposes into three (3) deliverable packages. The assignment includes the following activities:

Work plan and methodology: A detailed work plan incorporating the consultancy coordination, implementation-support and progress-monitoring schedule, information requirements, and data collection processes for Agrovizcaya Finca Viva. This deliverable must include the initial diagnostic scope of the biofactory and the ICA regulatory requirements applicable to its products, together with the stakeholder coordination arrangements with the company.
Integrated Management System (IMS) – Agrovizcaya Finca Viva
Review the current situation of the biofactory, identify and document gaps against the applicable Colombian regulatory requirements of the ICA, and recommend corrective actions.
Review, update, align, and prepare draft versions of the priority technical and operational documents agreed in the approved work plan — including:

A technical review of the existing biofactory layout, including recommendations to improve the arrangement of operational areas and process flows (covering reception, storage, composting, vermiculture, bokashi, biols, bioferments, plant extracts, packaging, and finished-product areas).
The review of personnel and material flow design and cross-contamination controls.
The review, update, alignment, and drafting of a Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Manual and an Integrated Management System Manual.
An Operations Manual and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Production flowcharts.
Programs for cleaning, disinfection, pest control, maintenance, and calibration.

Assess alignment and monitor the implementation of the traceability system and the quality assurance and control system, and review the progress reported on the agreed physical upgrades, recommending adjustments where needed.
Facilitate practical training for the Agrovizcaya team on the implementation and operation of the Integrated Management System.

Final report: consolidated closing report for Agrovizcaya Finca Viva, including the completed Integrated Management System documentation (documents reviewed, updated, aligned, or drafted under the approved work plan), physical upgrade plan, training records, and a consolidated draft technical file for the company's review and use in preparing the registration process before the ICA.
Out of scope
The following activities are not part of the scope of this consultancy for Agrovizcaya Finca Viva, unless separately assessed, quoted, and expressly approved by COMFAMA/GGGI:
Execution of civil works, facility upgrades, or modifications to the biofactory's infrastructure.
Supply, purchase, or installation of equipment, utensils, measuring instruments, or furniture.
Development of product formulations or new bioinput strains.
Laboratory testing (physicochemical, microbiological, or other analytical services).
Management, filing, or processing of registration applications before the ICA or other authorities, as well as payment of fees, licenses, or certifications.
Certification processes before certifying bodies (e.g., organic certification) and support during external audits.
Attendance and support during official ICA inspection, surveillance, and control visits, unless contracted as an additional scope.

Development or implementation of management systems other than the IMS agreed in the approved work plan (for example, ISO 9001, ISO 14001, or GLOBALG.A.P. certification), unless expressly agreed as part of the project.
Ongoing operational activities of the company (routine completion of records, daily execution of cleaning and disinfection programs, pest control).

Guarantee of registration, authorization, certification, or regulatory approval. For the sake of clarity, the consultant is not responsible for the outcome of the regulatory process, as approvals from the ICA or any other authority depend entirely on factors beyond the consultant's control.

Cross-Cutting Approach

Integrate principles of quality, traceability, biosafety, and continuous improvement into all technical, documentation, and implementation-support and progress-monitoring activities carried out for Agrovizcaya Finca Viva.

Review technical documentation complies with the applicable Colombian regulatory requirements of the Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) for organic fertilizers, soil conditioners, and agricultural bioinputs, and document identified gaps and recommended corrective actions to support the company's readiness for its registration process.

Maintain close coordination with Agrovizcaya Finca Viva, the Antioquia BioCompetitiva initiative, GGGI, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure the consistency and quality of the consultancy outputs.
REPORTING ARRANGEMENTS

The consultancy will report to the Bioeconomy Associate at GGGI Colombia, who is the contract supervisor and responsible for the formal acceptance of deliverables, following technical validation and acceptance by Agrovizcaya Finca Viva. The consultant's work progress will be monitored primarily through periodic review meetings for planning and weekly short face-to-face (or virtual) meetings for prioritizing activities, all of that previous consensus with the

All deliverables will be produced in Spanish, by GGGI's formatting requirements, and submitted with proof of editable file back-up (e.g., .docx, .pptx) in the GGGI SharePoint system. Where relevant, the consultant shall also provide raw data sets, research materials, and meeting notes related to the contractual objective.
EXPERTISE REQUIRED
Profile
(MANDATORY): Must be a Colombian citizen or a foreign national holding a valid work permit or visa to provide professional services in Colombia.

(MANDATORY): Professional degree in Agronomic Engineering, Agricultural or Agro-industrial Engineering, Industrial Microbiology, Chemical Engineering, Productivity and Quality Engineering, or related fields.

(MANDATORY): A postgraduate degree (Master's degree) in Integral Process Management, Integrated or Quality Management Systems, or related fields or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

(MANDATORY): A minimum of five (5) years of proven professional experience in the alignment, documentation, and management of integrated or quality management systems and Good Manufacturing Practices in agricultural, agro-industrial, or bioinput production facilities.

(DESIRABLE): Prior experience providing technical support for compliance-readiness processes with the Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) for the registration of producers of bioinputs, organic fertilizers, or soil conditioners.
(DESIRABLE): Proven experience conducting or supporting internal verification reviews and recommending corrective action plans in the agricultural or agro-industrial sectors.

SOCIAL AND SUSTAINABILITY SAFEGUARDS

GGGI as an institution abides by its project-level Sustainability and Safeguards Rules (SSR) for all projects, aligned with international standards for Environmental and Social Safeguards. The SSR is aligned with commonly recognized international standards for Environmental and Social Safeguards (ESS), i.e., the WB Performance Standard, that ensure project-level safeguarding of communities and people impacted by GGGI activities. GGGI has integrated project-level Environmental and Social Safeguards into its Project Cycle Management (PCM) with mandatory Preliminary Gender and Social Assessments and ESS Screening of all projects to identify and manage risks.

In addition, GGGI's Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Strategy 2021-2025 provides a framework toward achieving the principle of "Leaving No One Behind" in the transformation towards green growth, guiding GGGI's approaches to the mainstreaming of gender equality and poverty reduction in GGGI Colombia's Program. This also includes the implementation of the GGGI Gender Equality and Poverty Reduction Policy Markers on all projects. GGGI's Corporate Results Framework requires gender disaggregated indicators for participation in GGGI Capacity Building events.

Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
